GenLayer CEO Albert Castellana on why AI agent commerce needs neutral escrow instead of the legal system

"The way we look at this is that these agents will want to not lose the money."

"They cannot believe in the legal system, just because of the cost and the slowness of it."

"If I have some sort of smart contract that can be holding the money as an escrow, and also evaluating the evidence in a neutral way, then that would be the safest way for me to not lose the money and be able to actually do commerce."

"It's a court for the Internet."

"I deploy the contract, I have negotiated offchain something with another agent, the money is transacted, it's put into the escrow, then the other agent will do some piece of work, and then it will be a neutral party that will decide who's right."

"I really think it's gonna be a lot of the agents just deploying the contracts and trying to resolve between them, as we do with humans. Now the problem with humans is just that the legal system is very, very archaic."

This is insane! People's imagination for using memeFi is hitting new levels

You'll all be familiar with memes pumping real Penny Stonks, but not manipulating in game economies...

$RSTR is attempting to build a MicroStrategy-style treasury, except the reserve asset is Robin Hood hats inside Old School RuneScape

Why now? Because it's on Robonhood chain...

How it works:

1) $RSTR launched on pons against ETH
2) Every trade pays a 1% fee; of which 70% accrue to the token creator + 30% to pons
3) The RSTR operator claims the creator fees, converts the ETH into OSRS gold (assuming through Bond purchases?) uses that gold to buy Robin Hood hats
4) The hats are spread across multiple RuneScape accounts + withheld from sale
5) Removing hats from circulation pushes up the in-game market price, generating screenshots, attention and theoretically more $RSTR trading
6) More $RSTR trading produces more creator fees, funding further hat purchases

I wanted to check this against a third party source to see if this was actually happening... it is!

i) The GE tracker most players use in RuneScape is showing a spike from 700k RSGP to 4.5m now each hat in just two days
ii) The current price you can buy the hats for is > $4.5m RSGP... i checked and max bid to buy more of the supply actually in game (screenshot)

The main challenges to the process is that there's an element that needs to be off-chain with a human intermediary in using the ETH fees to purchase bonds + then in game currency for the RH hats

I'm not a lawyer but as long as they're purchasing the bonds through Jagex then it should be in compliance? Although not sure about intentional manipulation of in game economics?

Even so... if the accounts are banned it permanently removes the hats from the game and hence achieves the same outcome

You can capitalize on this by buying in game before it goes insane or more speculative through their token

Jagex would receive the revenue from Bond sales, but it's not public so we are unable to benefit from that side of the trade

Once again onchain mechanisms being used with memes to draw in more retail attention... this time from millions of RuneScape players!

A meme paired with a 3x short on $PONS is called "TAMPONS"... 

The mechanics for TAMPONS are pretty interesting:

1) Every $TAMPONS trade pays a 1% fee; part of that revenue is continuously routed into collateral backing a 3× short position on $PONS 

2) If PONS falls, the short generates a profit. The system periodically realizes part of it, then uses 75% of the proceeds to market-buy and burn TAMPONS

3) Flywheel: 

TAMPONS volume → fees → larger PONS short → realized profits if PONS falls → TAMPONS buybacks + burns

It isn’t a direct or fully redeemable hedge; holders don’t own the short or have a claim on its collateral. But structurally, TAMPONS converts trading activity & PONS downside into recurring buy pressure for itself

I'd be surprised if @loraclexyz doesn't kingmake this to drive awareness
